edges.description: Complement-sensitive red cells undergo lysis; suppression by C5 blockade supports terminal complement involvement.
Complement-mediated erythrocyte destruction contributes to the low hemoglobin concentration; concomitant marrow disease can also contribute in individual patients.
Intravascular lysis releases hemoglobin that can appear in urine. The reported urine discoloration occurred in the hemolytic clinical presentation.
intermediate_mechanisms: Release of cell-free hemoglobin into plasma
Renal filtration of circulating free hemoglobin

edges.description: Free GPI promotes complement activation in leukocyte and cell-line experiments.
Complement activation proceeds to terminal C5b-9 complex formation in the experimental inflammatory pathway.
C6/C7 depletion suppresses IL-1 beta secretion and replenishment restores it.

Enhanced IL-1 beta signaling is an inferred contributor to recurrent aseptic meningitis within the complement-associated autoinflammatory syndrome; the organ-level intermediates and contributions of other inflammatory mediators remain unresolved. The reported incomplete response to IL-1 blockade argues against attributing this manifestation solely to IL-1 beta.

Enhanced IL-1 beta signaling is an inferred contributor to urticaria within the complement-associated autoinflammatory syndrome; the organ-level intermediates and contributions of other inflammatory mediators remain unresolved.

Enhanced IL-1 beta signaling is an inferred contributor to arthralgia within the complement-associated autoinflammatory syndrome; the organ-level intermediates and contributions of other inflammatory mediators remain unresolved. The reported incomplete response to IL-1 blockade argues against attributing this manifestation solely to IL-1 beta.

Enhanced IL-1 beta signaling is an inferred contributor to fever within the complement-associated autoinflammatory syndrome; the organ-level intermediates and contributions of other inflammatory mediators remain unresolved.
Loss of the myeloid common deleted region is proposed to help the PIGT-deficient clone expand; the causal relationship remains unproven.
